requirements.verifier_assertion: test_valid_docx: /workspace/report.docx must exist, be non-empty, and open as a valid python-docx Document (v_docx_validity).

L2 code judge reads generated_code.py (or solve.py): it must be the actual runnable script that reads the Excel input and produces report.docx, not a stub or summary; graded on data extraction, presentation, chart logic, completeness, correctness.
test_page_dimensions: page width == 21.0 cm and page height == 29.7 cm (A4), tolerance 0.1cm.
test_page_margins: top/bottom margins 2.54 cm, left/right margins 3.0 cm (>=3 of 4 within 0.1cm).
test_body_font: the Normal style font name contains 'FangSong' and size is ~12pt.
test_paragraph_formatting: body paragraphs use 1.5x line spacing and a first-line indent ~24pt (score>=0.3).
test_table_present: at least 3 tables; a table with >=2 rows and >=2 columns; a bold header row.
test_chart_embedded: at least one inline shape (embedded image) in the document — the matplotlib yield-curve chart.
must_include: embed a yield curve chart made with matplotlib

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_content_structure: at least 3 of the five known section headings present in the document text (five required with level-2 headings).
L2/L3 judges expect section 4 to explain the discount function p(n)=exp(-n*r(n)); expected_data lists discount factors derived from a flat 10% curve.
L2 code judge / expected_data key values: flat 10% yield curve, spot volatility 12%, notional 100, partitions m=1, Ho-Lee constant maturity swap, years 0-12.
L2 code judge (code_data_extraction): code must open /workspace/data/input.xlsx and read from the furtherex1 worksheet's parameter regions.
Formatting requirement / expected_data: interest rates to 4 decimal places or as percentages, amounts to 2 decimal places; page numbers in footer.
